messages:
sam: FYI — incoming support ticket from VertexAI (customer). They want streaming chat responses that can emit structured chunks (JSON objects) intermittently while still supporting function/tool calls. Current ask landed in Support with a demo and logs. TL;DR: they have a live agent UI that needs partial structured results for progressive render + tool invocation when a frame indicates a call.

jordan: Customer is on an enterprise plan (~$120k ARR). They said this feature is a blocker for an upcoming pilot. High commercial urgency — asked for ETA on a supported contract-level behaviour.

maya: Thanks for the heads-up. Can you paste the support ticket summary and the demo payload? Need concrete acceptance criteria to scope. Is the ask: 1) stream NDJSON frames + 2) preserve semantics for fn calls mid-stream, or something else?

sam: Pasting the snippet they sent (redacted):

```
--stream frame 1--
{"type":"chunk","text":"User: How do I configure..."}
--stream frame 2--
{"type":"structure","schema":"{\\\"fields\\\":[...]}","data":{...}}
--stream frame 3--
{"type":"call","target":"browser.open","args":{"url":"https://..."}}
```

They say current API only reliably sends the final function call at the end of the session; they need mid-stream calls so the UI can open a helper tool before the final completion.

eli: Engineering note: runtime currently batches tokens and holds off finalizing function call objects until model completes or explicit stop. We can surface partial function-call intents by emitting a delta event when the decoder emits a special token sequence, but we'll need to update the stream framing and validation in SDKs. Main risks: 1) breaking existing clients that assume single final call, 2) ordering guarantees under batching.

maya: Good. Proposed acceptance criteria (draft):
- server can emit multiple structured frames in a single streaming response (NDJSON or equivalent)
- a frame with "type":"call" triggers immediate client-visible tool invocation (documented contract)
- backward compatible: clients not parsing frames keep receiving plain text fallback
- SDKs (python/js) expose an event hook for partial frames
- integration tests + perf regression <5% p99 latency increase

Can someone give rough dev estimate and risk list? Also note: we should decide design for idempotency if calls retry.

eli: Rough estimate: 3-4 sprints to implement API surface + SDK changes + tests (2 engs full time), plus 1 sprint for rollout, feature flag, and docs. Risks: cache/batch side effects, additional memory for buffering structured frames, need to add opt-in header/param for contract. I recommend opt-in flag (e.g., "stream_structured_frames=true") to avoid immediate breakage.

sam: Customer prefers no opt-in (just works) but will accept opt-in for pilot if ETA is faster. They want a canary by mid-quarter.

infra-bot: Note: there is an existing internal experiment branch `stream-frames-v2` with basic framing logic (PR #4212). It has unit tests but not SDK hooks. CI shows 2 failing flaky tests.

maya: Plan: 1) create a backlog ticket (product/roadmap) with the acceptance criteria above, classify as P1 for pilot support, 2) tag eng-runtime and SDK teams, 3) request canary from infra once PRs are green, 4) prepare a short SDK migration guide.\nAction items: @eli to draft tech spec by EOD Tue; @sam to attach the full support thread and demo video to the ticket; @jordan to confirm commercial timeline with the customer; I'll own rollout/acceptance criteria and decide on opt-in vs default after eng spec.

jordan: I'll push for pilot opt-in if it shortens ETA. Customer open to pilot flag for first 30 days. :thumbsup:

sam: Attached ticket and demo link in the new backlog card. Repro steps included.

eli: Will start tech spec, will call out API contract options (NDJSON vs SSE vs chunked JSON) and recommended signal tokens for call frames.

maya: Great — marking this thread for intake sync tomorrow 10:30am. If anyone has constraints (regulatory, KMS, private deploy) that change feasibility, flag now.

jordan: No regulatory blockers on their side, they run in our hosted offering.

sam: Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
